page: Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is an x86_64 virtual server positioned within the general-purpose Cloud Compute family. The configuration includes 8 shared Intel vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with architectural support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instructions. The instance incorporates 32 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 640 GB of local NVMe SSD space, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core execution on stress-ng and Geekbench registers in the lower tiers, reflecting the shared processor allocation and modest 2.0 GHz clock rate. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU and stress-ng multi-core maintain middle-tier throughput, demonstrating effective parallel thread scaling. Software compilation via Clang and ray tracing tests show average results. In-memory performance is highlighted by Redis reaching 7.55 million SET operations per second, though large-block uncached memory write bandwidth is limited at 14.02 GB/sec.

Regarding qualitative resource efficiency, the vc2-8c-32gb offers a practical balance of substantial RAM and integrated high-capacity NVMe storage relative to its shared compute tier. The shared vCPU model introduces performance tradeoffs under persistent compute saturation, making it less viable for CPU-bound high-frequency workloads. The hardware profile is appropriate for general-purpose application hosting, in-memory caching layers, staging platforms, CI/CD runners, and relational database systems that rely on bundled NVMe storage and balanced memory.
description: Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 8 shared Intel vCPUs, 32 GB of system RAM, and 640 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage. Built on an x86_64 architecture using 4 physical cores at 2.0 GHz with 16 MB of L3 cache, it delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Benchmark results highlight modest single-core throughput alongside middle-tier multi-core and compilation performance, with Redis achieving 7.55 million operations per second. The shared core model and limited uncached write bandwidth represent tradeoffs under sustained computational load, but the absence of a GPU and the provision of generous local storage make it cost-efficient for general infrastructure. It is suited for web applications, caching tiers, build nodes, and moderate database workloads.
